docs(changelog): restack coverage entries
Co-Authored-By: Kimchi <noreply@kimchi.dev>

fix(review): protocol v2 pins + docs_gate resolution interplay
A linear extension (a push whose covered commits keep their SHAs: some
joinable record's tip is an ancestor of the new tip) is the ordinary
fix-push, not a restack. restack-b's incremental path swallowed it and
skipped the resolver call entirely (_no_evidence), so the prior doc
finding judged 'unverified' and a fixed push re-blocked forever -- the
resolver is the only clearing path and must still run over the union
(spec: Incremental review and verdict combination). True restacks
(rewritten SHAs) keep the never-spend-a-resolver-call behaviour.

Also: the intent-extra tests pinned protocol_version 1; records are v2
since restack-a, so the pins move to 2 and the v2 round-trip shape.

Co-Authored-By: Kimchi <noreply@kimchi.dev>

Merge branch 'integration/restack-coverage' into piece/restack-b

[restack-b] incremental range reduction + verdict combination
A push whose range is only partially covered (the normal case: a restack
plus genuinely new work) reviews only the uncovered commits and combines
the incremental review with the prior verdict: worst-of verdict, union of
findings deduped by finding-id, every prior finding still re-anchored
against the new tip. A quiet incremental run clears nothing -- only a
resolver verdict with added-side evidence clears a prior, and an
unverified prior stays blocking. Commits without a patch-id (binary/merge/
empty) enter the incremental range individually when uncovered, never
widening it. The reviewer prompt states this is a partial re-review after
a restack, so it Greps for context rather than assuming it has the full
change. Records superseded by the new coverage are replaced only after
the new record exists.

  commits' own diffs drive the review; covered paths are never re-reviewed
